result.title: Your Benchmark Is an Empirical Measure Over Difficulty
result.summary: A benchmark is not merely a collection of test questions; it naturally induces an empirical measure over difficulty. In this work, we develop this measure-based view of benchmark evaluation. This perspective allows us to identify and formalize two central failure modes: measure mismatch, where the benchmark difficulty distribution differs from the intended difficulty distribution, and coverage gaps, where uncovered regions along the difficulty axis prevent benchmarks from detecting meaningful localized training progress. We propose two diagnostic metrics that capture these two failure modes and provide rigorous theoretical guarantees. Empirically, we analyze 25 popular benchmarks spanning 7 domains using carefully estimated item difficulties. Our results show that many benchmarks implicitly overweight certain difficulty regions, so their leaderboard conclusions should be interpreted with caution; others leave substantial portions of the difficulty axis uncovered, limiting their ability to monitor the model improvement process. Finally, we turn diagnosis into action by introducing BenchFill, a simple difficulty-targeted item rewriting algorithm that effectively reduces local coverage gaps.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把基准视为难度轴上的经验测度，形式化「测度错配」与「覆盖缺口」两种失效模式，提出两个诊断指标，分析 25 个跨 7 领域基准，并提出按难度定向改写的 BenchFill 算法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其难度分布与局部覆盖视角可能为 LVR 评测提供参照：若把难度轴换成推理步数或计算量，可用于核查 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的收益是否被基准覆盖、局部训练进步能否被检出，但难度估计是否适配多模态推理成本维度仍需核查。
